topics.name: The biosphere
subtopics: The biosphere includes the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere, all living organisms and dead organic matter
The seven life processes: nutrition, growth, reproduction, respiration, excretion, sensitivity and movement
Requirements for sustaining life: energy, gases, water, soil and favourable temperatures
Living things are adapted to the environment in which they live
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Biodiversity
subtopics: Classification of living things by shared characteristics; five Kingdoms: Bacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plants and Animals
Classification hierarchy from Kingdom, Phylum/Division, Class, Order, Family and Genus to Species
Vertebrates: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals and their distinguishing characteristics
Invertebrates: Arthropoda (insects, arachnids, crustaceans) and Mollusca
Diversity of plants: plants with and without seeds; Angiosperms and Gymnosperms
Monocotyledons and dicotyledons differ in roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds; emphasise South African examples
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Sexual reproduction
subtopics: Structure of a flower: stamens, stigma, style, ovary, petals and sepals
Pollination by wind, water and pollinators; adaptations of flowers; importance of pollinators for food crops
Fertilisation in Angiosperms: pollen tube, fusion of sex cells, seed and fruit formation; seed dispersal
Human reproduction: puberty, male and female reproductive organs, fertilisation, menstruation and pregnancy
Contraception (condoms) and prevention of HIV/AIDS and other STDs; consequences of early sexual activity
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Variation
subtopics: A species is a group of living things of the same type that can reproduce together
Variation is the differences between individuals of the same species
Inherited variation in humans such as height and tongue-rolling
topics.lessons_off_reason: Life and Living strand (Life Sciences, not one of the 6 subjects)

topics.name: Introduction to the Periodic Table of Elements
subtopics: The Periodic Table as a classification system for the elements, devised by Mendeleev in the 1860s
Arrangement of metals (left), non-metals (far right) and semi-metals (between)
Each element has a name, symbol, atomic number and position on the Periodic Table
Properties of metals, semi-metals and non-metals

topics.name: Properties of materials
subtopics: Physical properties (boiling and melting points, electrical and heat conductivity) determine suitability for a use
Other factors such as cost, colour and texture in choosing materials
Environmental impact of producing and using materials such as metals, plastics and fuels

topics.name: Separating mixtures
subtopics: A mixture is made of two or more substances with different physical properties
Separation methods: hand sorting, sieving, filtration, magnets, evaporation, distillation and chromatography
Sorting and recycling materials; responsible waste disposal and consequences of poor waste management

topics.name: Acids, bases and neutrals
subtopics: Tastes of substances: salty, sweet, sour and bitter (not all substances are safe to taste)
Properties of acids and bases, with household examples; neutrals
Acid-base indicators: using red and blue litmus paper to classify substances

topics.name: Remediation, revision and consolidation
subtopics: Remediation, revision and consolidation of Matter and Materials content

topics.name: Sources of energy
subtopics: Energy is needed to make everything work, move or live
Non-renewable sources (fossil fuels, nuclear fuels) and renewable sources (hydro power, wind, sunlight, biofuel)

topics.name: Potential and kinetic energy
subtopics: Potential energy as stored energy, including energy in food measured in joules (no calculations)
Kinetic energy as the energy of a moving body
Potential and kinetic energy in mechanical, thermal, electrical and biological systems
Law of conservation of energy; energy transfer within and between systems

topics.name: Heat transfer
subtopics: Heating as transfer of energy from a hotter to a cooler body until temperatures are equal
Conduction; conductors and insulators of heat
Convection and convection currents in air and water
Radiation; shiny surfaces reflect and dark surfaces absorb radiant heat

topics.name: Insulation and energy saving
subtopics: Heat loss and gain through conduction, convection and radiation
Using insulating materials in cool boxes, ceilings, clothing and blankets
Conserving heat energy in buildings; energy-efficient indigenous South African homes

topics.name: Energy transfer to surroundings
subtopics: Useful and ‘wasted’ energy outputs of appliances, tools, vehicles and machines
Output energy is always less than input energy; wasted energy escapes as heat and/or sound

subtopics: Remediation, revision and consolidation of Energy and Change content

topics.name: Relationship of the Sun to the Earth
subtopics: The Earth spins on an axis tilted at 23,5°; tilt causes changing intensity of solar energy and the four seasons
Day length varies with the seasons
Solar energy sustains life on Earth through plants
Stored solar energy: formation of coal, oil and gas (fossil fuels) as a non-renewable resource

topics.name: Relationship of the Moon to the Earth
subtopics: The Moon revolves around the Earth in its orbit
Gravity depends on mass and distance; gravity holds the Earth and Moon in their orbits
Tides caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity; spring tides; shoreline ecosystems
